What is LodgeOps?: LodgeOps is Malvavisco's administration software for lodges. It keeps bookings, rooms, activities, kitchen work, charges, payments and reports in a shared staff workspace.
What kind of lodge is it for?: It is designed for places that sell stays alongside activities, meals or extras and need to coordinate people and equipment. We can walk through your own operation in a demo to see whether it fits.
Can we manage more than one property?: The app supports properties within a workspace, and a person who belongs to more than one workspace can switch between them. Each property's rooms, rates and resources are configured in Settings.
Which languages does the staff app suppo: The staff interface follows the workspace's English or Spanish setting. Some server-generated labels and API error messages remain in English.
How do we get started?: A workspace is created by the operator, then the team configures business information, properties, rooms, rates, services, staff, resources and communication settings. There is no self-service public sign-up or free trial today.
Can a booking use different rooms on dif: Yes. A stay can use one room plan for the whole visit or a split assignment by night. Each night must have enough room capacity.
How does LodgeOps prevent double booking: The app checks room availability and capacity when preparing the booking and rechecks commitments when saving changes. Unavailable rooms cannot be selected for that stay.
Are activities scheduled when they are s: No. Buying a service adds the charge but does not reserve a guide, horse, boat or other equipment. Staff schedule a concrete session and assign resources afterwards; that scheduling does not charge the guest again.
What can we see in the calendar?: Places, Crew and Assets views show rooms, people and equipment by week, month or season. Crew and asset entries represent actual scheduled assignment times.
Does LodgeOps connect to Booking.com or: No. LodgeOps is not a channel manager, and OTA connections are not part of the current product. Ask us about the availability calendar feeds that are supported.
How does the kitchen know what to prepar: Booking-linked point-of-sale orders can create preparation tickets for routed products. The kitchen also has meal planning, checklists and supply receipts, with dietary context for guests.
Can we schedule guides, horses and boats: Yes. Purchased activities can be scheduled for a specific time with guides and assets. The app checks concrete overlaps and resource requirements before committing assignments.
What can different staff roles see?: LodgeOps has eleven staff roles, including sales, operations, coordinator, guide, kitchen, housekeeping and finance. Navigation follows capabilities, and the API independently enforces access.
Can LodgeOps send guest reminders?: Versioned English and Spanish templates, reminder rules and delivery history are implemented. Guest templates must be published and a sender configured; production email delivery has not yet been verified.
Does LodgeOps work without internet?: No. Offline operation is not currently supported. The staff app requires a connection to the server to read current availability and save changes safely.
Which payment methods can staff record?: Staff can record manual cash, bank-transfer and card-terminal payments, allocate them to charges, reverse them and attach private receipt evidence.
Can guests pay online?: Not yet as a production service. Mercado Pago links for Argentina and ARS are implemented, but real provider checkout, notification and settlement acceptance remain pending.
Is the printable invoice a fiscal docume: LodgeOps can print a numbered snapshot of a booking's charges and payments. Local fiscal certification and accounting-provider integration are separate work.
How are different currencies reported?: Reports keep amounts separated by currency. Workspace base currency and dated exchange-rate snapshots support some converted views, but cross-currency payment settlement is not implemented.
Can we export reports?: Several reports support CSV or XLSX detail exports, including taxes, guests, geography and feedback. Some export headings and server-provided labels remain in English.
How are staff permissions protected?: The app uses role-based permissions that are checked by the server. Two-factor authentication is available but optional; access also follows workspace and property scope.
How are receipt attachments handled?: Private payment attachments are quarantined for scanning before download. A running scanner is required for that workflow, so deployment setup matters.
Can guests sign waivers or upload identi: Not yet. Staff can manage waiver templates and see identity-document lists, but guest-side signing and upload are not implemented.
What is not included yet?: Current limits include OTA/channel-manager connections, fully offline use, package pricing and itineraries, fiscal integrations, walk-in restaurant table management and production-accepted online checkout.
Are the product screenshots real?: The screens show the LodgeOps staff app filled with fictional sample lodge data. They illustrate current workflows without exposing a real guest or customer.
